minutes.headline: Committee voted to cancel April vacation week 2020 and keep remote learning; two equity policies approved.
minutes.summary: Remote School Committee meeting during the COVID-19 closure. The committee discussed the superintendent's recommendation to cancel April vacation and approved a revised calendar, then approved two policies on third reading. The business manager updated on the bus contract, hiring and purchasing freezes, and the FY21 budget timeline, and a budget public hearing date was discussed.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment on agenda items; none from the public.
Second call for public comment; none received from the public.

votes.motion: Approve the revised 2019-2020 school calendar cancelling April vacation and continuing remote learning
Approve policies 5218 and 5218.01 as read, third reading

budget_items.what_was_said: Thirteen districts are approaching the bus vendor together about paying part of the remaining contract; the state guidance is to negotiate operating costs, not pay in full.
The district remains in a hiring and purchasing freeze; the town manager was contacted about possible last-minute purchases from surplus funds.
The business manager thought the nurses' work for the Board of Health would be reimbursable as an emergency expense.
The town is restarting FY21 budgets on a level-service basis, and new positions proposed on March 11th are being reviewed.

decisions.decision: Budget public hearing to be scheduled on either the 27th or the 29th of April; the superintendent's office will survey members.
Next meeting stays on the 15th, with the Springfield trip and a principals' update on the agenda.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted by roll call to cancel April vacation week and continue remote learning under a revised 2019-2020 calendar.
The committee approved policies 5218 and 5218.01 on third reading by roll call.
The business manager said thirteen districts are approaching the bus vendor together about paying part of the remaining contract, with state guidance to negotiate operating costs.
The district remains in a hiring and purchasing freeze, and the town is restarting FY21 budgets on a level-service basis.
A budget public hearing is to be set for the 27th or the 29th of April, after the superintendent's office surveys members.

why_it_matters: Cancelling April vacation changes the school calendar for families, and the bus contract talks decide whether the district pays for service it is not using.

The FY21 budget restarting on a level-service basis means new positions proposed in March are under review, so what the schools can add next year is not settled and the budget hearing is where residents can comment.
